rows.question: In Dharamdeo v. Bijarat, was the land reform law within the State legislature's competence?
rows.answer:

Provisions: Constitution Art.31A (2) [1]

rows.question: Explain section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
rows.answer:
Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines cheating as occurring when a person, by deceiving another, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the deceived person to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the deceived person to do or omit to do something which they would not do or omit if not deceived. This act or omission must cause or be likely to cause damage or harm to the deceived person in body, mind, reputation, or property [1]. A dishonest concealment of facts is also considered a deception within the meaning of this section [1].

Illustrations provided under the section include scenarios such as deceiving someone into lending money on credit, selling counterfeit goods, and inducing someone to advance money based on false promises of delivery or performance of a contract [1].

Provisions: BNS s.318 [1]
This is legal information, not legal advice.

rows.question: What is dowry death and how is it punished?
rows.answer:
Dowry death is defined as the death of a woman caused by any burns or bodily injury, or occurring otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, where it is shown that she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry [1][2].

The punishment for causing a dowry death is imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life [1][2].

Provisions: BNS s.80 [1]; IPC s.304B [2]
This is legal information, not legal advice.

rows.question: What counts as organised crime?
rows.answer:
Organised crime includes activities such as kidnapping, robbery, vehicle theft, extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, economic offences, cyber-crimes, trafficking of persons, drugs, weapons or illicit goods or services, human trafficking for prostitution or ransom, by any person or a group of persons acting in concert [1]. For the purposes of this sub-section, "organised crime syndicate" means a group of two or more persons who, acting either singly or jointly, as a syndicate or gang indulge in any continuing unlawful activity [1].

Provisions: BNS s.111 [1]
This is legal information, not legal advice.

rows.question: When is culpable homicide not murder?
rows.answer:
Culpable homicide is not murder if it is committed without premeditation in a sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel and without the offender’s ill-will towards the person whose death is caused [1]. Additionally, it is not murder if the offender, being a public servant or aiding a public servant acting for the advancement of public justice, exceeds the powers given to him by law, and causes death by doing an act which he, in good faith, believes to be lawful and necessary for the due discharge of his duty as such public servant and without ill-will towards the person whose death is caused [1]. Furthermore, it is not murder if the offender in the exercise in good faith of the right of private defence of person or property, exceeds the power given to him by law and causes the death of the person against whom he is exercising such right of defence without premeditation, and without any intention of doing more harm than is necessary for the purpose of such defence [1].

Provisions: BNS s.101 [1], Exception 2 and Exception 3; BNS s.101, Exception 4 [1] This is legal information, not legal advice.

rows.question: Is a repeat offence punished more severely?
rows.answer:
Stalking under the BNS is defined as follows: Any man who—
(i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or
(ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic communication,
commits the offence of stalking [1]. The punishment for stalking on first conviction is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine. On a second or subsequent conviction, the punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine [1].

A repeat offence of stalking is punished more severely. According to BNS s.71, whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 64, 65, 66 or 70 and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death [2].

Provisions: BNS s.78 [1]; BNS s.71 [2]
This is legal information, not legal advice.
